MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing
  Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  May 13, 2025
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ruesch at
5:00 p.m., on May 13, 2025, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on May 8, 2025, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at the
Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray Community
and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Vasquez (arrived 5:02pm)
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Ruesch

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Elaine Lister, City Manager
  Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley, City Attorney
  Ellis Chang, Director of Administrative Services
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

 CLOSED SESSION

 CS1.  Conference with Legal Counsel: Threat to Critical Infrastructure Controls or
  Information Relating to Cybersecurity. Consultation with City Attorney and Director
  of Information Technology David Meyer

 CS2.  Conference with Legal Counsel – Existing Litigation Paragraph (1) of subdivision (d) of
  Section 54956.9 Janice Kronik Gath, et. al v. Mission Viejo OCSC Case No. 30-2024-
  01376969-CU-MC-CJC

 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

City Council Minutes  1  May 13, 2025
  At the hour of 5:01pm Mayor Ruesch recessed to Closed Session. At the hour of 6:02pm Mayor
 Ruesch reconvened the meeting with all five Council Members present.

 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

 City Attorney Curley announced that Closed Session No.2 was not discussed and shall be continued,
 and Closed Session No.1 was discussed with no reportable action.

 INVOCATION: Mayor Ruesch

 PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

 PRESENTATIONS

 P1.  Proclaim May 2025 Top Be Jewish American Heritage Month

  Mayor Ruesch presented proclamation to Dr. Mark Cymerint and Jennifer Vigiletti.

 P2.  Recognize the Community of Character Committee for Receiving the Promising
  Practices Award

  Mayor Ruesch presented proclamation to Council Member Trish Kelley, Committee
  Chairwoman Stacey Cartledge and President Ethan Williams.

 Mayor Ruesch provided two updates. The first being the grand reopening of Fire Station 24 on
 Thursday, July 17, 2025, with more details to come nearer the time. And secondly, he addressed the
 upcoming election process regarding the staggering of terms. He stated that one can submit their
 comments on the city’s website and encouraged residents to share their comments pertaining to the
 staggering of districts for the 2026 Election.

 PUBLIC COMMENTS

 Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Played an excerpt of a recording of Mayor Ruesch’s outburst towards her public
 comments from April 22, Council meeting. Commented on how the Council abuses and intimidates
 public speakers and cuts off their time at the podium yet does not enforce the same policy for Council
 Members. Spoke of how the Mayor misled the public due to his limited knowledge of the flock system.
 How he was chosen as Mayor over Cynthia because he has the same viewpoint as most of the Council,
 and concluded by stating the Mayor did not even have the decency to close the meeting in memory of
 former Council Member Gail Reavis who passed away last month.

 Tom Moore, M.V.: Thanked the Mayor for being responsive to the community with regards to the
 upcoming elections and also thanked the City Manager for her update on the Steinmart property. He
 suggested the Memorial Day Celebration be moved from Kershaw Gardens to the Veterans Memorial
 at the Norman P. Murray Center and for the City to involve the community, schools, and bands in
 Veteran events.

City Council Minutes  2  May 13, 2025
  Amy Buch, M.V.: Thanked the Council for recognizing and proclaiming Jewish American Heritage
 Month and how much that means to her.

 Lynn Hillman, M.V.: Spoke on the flock cameras and voiced her concerns of resident’s privacy with
 this surveillance system in Mission Viejo. She questioned the Council’s decision on the need for this
 system in such a safe city.

 Carlos Pianelli, M.V.: Thanked Council Member Vasquez for the opportunity of meeting with
 Congresswoman Young Kim. He spoke of the constitutional crisis, due process as a right and not a
 privilege, of ICE (Immigration and Customs Enforcement), democracy and referred to the Character
 word of the month ~ Moral Courage.

 Saga Conroy, M.V.: Spoke on the Love Mission Viejo Day event this Saturday, May 17, and
 encouraged residents to view the website and sign up for a volunteer project.

 Stacy Holmes, M.V.: Voiced his concerns on Capistrano Unified School District Board Member Judy
 Bullockus use of the N-word, and the lack of an apology. He questioned Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum,
 Council Member Goodell and Council Member Kelley of their continued support of Judy Bullockus.

 Sam Lewis, M.V.: Pastor Lewis stated that May 1st was National Day of Prayer where many churches
 came together and prayed for each and every Council Member. He showed his appreciation and
 gratitude for each Council Members and asked the Lord to give them wisdom and guidance in making
 the right decisions in leading our City.

 Randall Simmons, M.V.: Voiced his concerns on Law Enforcement and ICE. He urged the Council
 to minimize ICE in Mission Viejo. Questioned the motivation for the installation of Flock cameras
 and who will control the data. Lastly, he encouraged establishing oversight of the Flock System.

 Peggy O’Neill, M.V.: Complemented and thanked Mayor Ruesch for addressing the problem of
 mosquitoes. She also touched on Immigration, how this country is made up of immigrants and how
 the immigrants arriving today are no different to the immigrants that arrived in her great-grandfathers
 time, hoping for a better life.

 Fiona Carroll, M.V.: Shared her concerns of Judy Bullockus representing Character Counts at
 Bathgate Elementary School.

 Kelly Anderson, M.V.: Spoke of the recent Capistrano Unified School District Board Meeting
 pertaining to Judy Bullockus’ racial slur.

 Elijah Saine, M.V.: Spoke on behalf of the Community of Character Committee on the Character
 Word of the Month “Moral Courage”.

 Roger Perez, M.V.: Voiced his concerns regarding Judy Bullockus’ use of the N-word and asked that
 she recuse herself from participating in Bathgate Elementary School’s Character Counts Program.
 Stated that as a parent, we need to set an example for our children that racial slurs are not acceptable
 so, he started a petition to remove Judy Bullockus from Bathgate Elementary School and asked the
 Council to sign his petition.
City Council Minutes  3  May 13, 2025
  Mike Maiolo, M.V.: Spoke on the Love Mission Viejo Day event on Saturday, May 17, and thanked
 the City Council for allowing this event to take place.

 CONSENT CALENDAR

 Items 25 and 26 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

 Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to approve the
 Consent Calendar outlined below.

 On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

 AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
 NOES:  None
 ABSENT:  None

 1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of April 22, 2025, as presented.

 2.  General Check Register dated April 11, 2025, in the Amount of $2,595,767.54

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 3.  General Check Register Dated April 18, 2025, in the Amount of $2,914,167.16

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 4.  General Check Register Dated April 25, 2025, in the Amount of $850,982.09

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 5.  Golf Check Register Dated April 11, 2025, in the Amount of $14,091.31

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 6.  Golf Check Register Dated April 18, 2025, in the Amount of $254,136.76

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 7.  Golf Check Register Dated April 25, 2025, in the Amount of $26,397.71

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 8.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March 2025

  Received and filed.
City Council Minutes  4  May 13, 2025
  9.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for March 2025

  Received and filed.

 10.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March
  2025

  Received and filed.

 11.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for March 2025

  Received and filed.

 12.  Transmittal of Pre-PARE Trustee Report for the quarter ending March 31,2025

  Received and filed the accompanying Pre-PARE Trustee Report for the quarter ending March
  31.2025.

 13.  Enterprise Storage Arrays Support Renewal

  Approved 3-year support renewal for PureStorage enterprise storage arrays through CDW-G
  in the amount of $107,262.

 14.  Website Hosting, Support, and Development Services

  (1) Approved third amendment to the existing agreement with Interpersonal Frequency for
  website hosting services, development, and support for the period of June 1, 2025 – May 31,
  2026 (Year 2), increasing the contract by the amount of $128,282; and (2) authorized the
  issuance of a purchase order to Interpersonal Frequency in the amount of $128,282.

 15.  Secure Data Backup and Recovery Appliances

  Approved purchase of the ObjectFirst OOTBI secure data backup storage appliances,
  including 5 years of support and maintenance, from Golden Star Technology in the amount
  of $107,361.

 16.  Second Amendment to the Waste Disposal Agreement Between the County of Orange
  and the City of Mission Viejo

  (1) Adopted Resolution 25-10 Approving a Second Amendment to the 2009 Waste Disposal
  Agreement with the County of Orange; and (2) authorized the Mayor to execute the Second
  Amendment on behalf of the City of Mission Viejo.

City Council Minutes  5  May 13, 2025
  17.  2025-2027 School Crossing Guard Services

  Approved the First Amendment with American Guard Services, Inc., to modify certain terms
  of the contract contingent upon approval of the Fiscal Year 2025-2027 budget.

 18.  MV Shuttle Operations

  Approved the Sixth Amendment with LAZ Parking California, Inc. for the operation of the
  MV Shuttle contingent upon approval of the FY 2025-2026 Operating Budget.

 19.  High-Intensity Activated Crosswalk (HAWK) Traffic Signal Installation & Intersection
  Improvements Intersection of Olympiad Road and Lake Mission Viejo/Youth Athletic
  Park - CIP 24259

  (1) Adopted Resolution 25-11 Amending the Fiscal Year 2024/2025 Budget for Costs
  Related to CIP 24259; and (2) awarded the construction contract for the subject project to
  Select Electric, Inc. (A25-09) in the amount of $420,645.00.

 20.  Mission Viejo Trash and Runoff Abatement Project (TRAP) – 2025 Measure M2 ECP
  Grant Application

  Adopted Resolution 25-12 Authorizing an Application for Funds for the Environmental
  Cleanup, Tier 1 Grant Program under Orange County Local Transportation Ordinance No. 3
  for the Mission Viejo Trash and Runoff Abatement Projects.

 21.  World Cup Soccer Fields Security Lighting (CIP 339) – Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk
  to record Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the Faithful
  Performance and Payment Bonds one year and thirty- five (35) days respectively, after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed
  with the City; and (4) authorized the payment of the final retention of $9,629.50, thirty-five
  (35) days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

 22.  Professional Services Agreements for On-Call CEQA Consulting Services

  Approved four Professional Services Agreements for On-Call CEQA Consulting Services,
  awarded to: (1) Ascent Environmental, Inc. (A25-10); (2) De Novo Planning Group (A25-
  11); (3) Dudek (A25-12); and (4) Michael Baker International (A25-13), each in an amount
  not to exceed $500,000 annually for a term of three (3) years, and authorized the City
  Manager to execute each of the four Agreements.

 23.  Draft Fiscal Year 2025-2029 Consolidated Plan, including the Fiscal Year 2025-2026
  Action Plan for the Expenditure of Fiscal Year 2025-2026 CDBG Funds and the 2025-
  2029 Orange County Regional Assessment of Fair Housing.

City Council Minutes  6  May 13, 2025
   Adopted Resolution 25-13 Approving the City’s Draft Fiscal Year 2025-2029 Consolidated
  Plan, including the Fiscal Year 2025-2026 Action Plan for the Expenditure of Fiscal Year
  2025-2026 CDBG Funds and the 2025-2029 Orange County Regional Assessment of Fair
  Housing, and authorizing submission of the plan to the United States Department of Housing
  and Urban Development.

 24.  Authorization Resolution to Allow the City Manager, or Their Designee, to Execute all
  Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA) Documents

  Adopted Resolution 25-14 Authorizing the City Manager, or their Designee, to Execute all
  Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA) documents.

 27.  Graffiti Removal, Steam Cleaning, Painting and Sealing Services – Bonanza Steam
  Cleaning, Inc.

  (1) Approved Thirteenth Amendment to the existing maintenance contract with Bonanza
  Steam Cleaning, Inc for the subject services; and (2) authorized a Change Order to the
  existing Purchase Order for Bonanza Steam Cleaning, Inc. in an amount not to exceed
  $20,000.00.

 28.  Annual Routine Playground, Parkland, and Facility Infrastructure Maintenance and
  Repairs – Jamey Clark, Inc.

  (1) Approved Seventh Amendment to the existing maintenance contract with Jamey Clark,
  Inc for the subject services; and (2) authorized a Change Order to the existing Purchase Order
  for Jamey Clark, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $70,000.00.

 29.  Annual Routine Monthly Landscape Maintenance - Contract Area 3

  (1) Approved Seventh Amendment to the existing maintenance contract with Nieves
  Landscape, Inc.; (2) authorized issuance of a change order to the existing Purchase Order for
  Landscape Contract Area 3 to Nieves Landscape, Inc. in an amount not to exceed
  $100,000.00.

 ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

 25.  Revisions to City of Mission Viejo Personnel Policies

  Human Recourses Manager Monique Goetz presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelly, to adopt
  Resolution 25-15 Providing for the Revisions to Select Personnel Policies.

City Council Minutes  7  May 13, 2025
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

 26.  Annual Routine Tree Trimming Contract

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services presented the staff report.

  Scott Griffiths, Irvine: Spoke on the longstanding maintenance contract that the City has not
  gone out to bid on for the past 26 years. He asked the Council to give other companies the
  chance and opportunity to bid as well.

  Council Members made various comments.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelly, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to (1) approve
  Thirty-second Amendment to the existing contract with West Coast Arborists, Inc. for the period
  of July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2027 in the amount of $2,918,547.00; and (2) authorize issuance
  of a purchase order to West Coast Arborists, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2025 through June 30,
  2026, in an amount not to exceed $1,434,835.00 pending adoption of the 2025-2027 budget by
  City Council.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

 PUBLIC HEARINGS

 30.  Compliance with New Legal Obligations re: Public Hearing on City of Mission Viejo
  Vacancies, and Recruitment & Retention Efforts (Assembly Bill 2561/Government
  Code Section 3502.3).

  Human Recourses Manager Monique Goetz presented the staff report.

  Mayor Ruesch opened and closed the Public Hearing at 7:37 pm as there were no requests to
  speak on this item.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to adopt
  Resolution 25-16 Adopting a Public Hearing and Reporting on Vacancies, and Recruitment,
  & Retention Efforts Policy and Amending the City Council Policy Manual.

City Council Minutes  8  May 13, 2025
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

 NEW BUSINESS

 31.  Establish General Fund Target and Minimum Reserve Levels for 2025-27 Budget Cycle

  Director of Administrative Services Ellis Chang presented the staff report.

  Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Spoke on the Library and asked for further information, at a future
  Council meeting, regarding the library becoming self-sufficient and no longer getting the
  same allocation from the budget as in the past. She asked the Council to reconsider the city’s
  support for the library.

  City Manager Lister stated that around 2017, subsidies were reduced at all City facilities,
  however, the Council can consider changing that moving forward. City Attorney Curley
  added that the library does receive funds from the County, and Director Chang mentioned
  that the library is projected to receive approx. 3.6 million of revenue from property taxes.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Ruesch, to adopt
  Resolution 25-17 Establishing General Fund Target and Minimum Reserve Levels for the
  2025-2027 Budget Cycle.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

 CITY MANAGER REPORTS

 No report given.

 CITY ATTORNEY REPORTS

 No report given.

 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

 32.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234
City Council Minutes  9  May 13, 2025
   By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

 Council Member Goodell

 Council Member Goodell spoke of flock cameras and the reason they are a consideration is due to the
 increase in property and vehicle crimes. With many neighboring cities also having flock cameras, it
 enables the city to solve crimes and keep residents safe. Commented on the situation pertaining to
 Judy Bullockus, and concluded by thanking Mike Maiolo and the Love Mission Viejo group and
 encouraged all residents to participate this coming Saturday.

 Council Member Kelley

 Council Member Kelley highlighted upcoming events; Love Mission Viejo Day, Saturday, May 17,
 and Memorial Day Ceremony at City Hall, Monday, May 26. She outlined various events she attended
 during the past couple of weeks; SCAG Conference (Southern California Association of
 Governments), Wildlife presentation at the Norman P. Murray Center, Third Grade Environmental
 Fair, Earth Day/Arbor Day, Family Arts Day at the Potocki Center for the Arts, Teen Wellness Summit
 at Capistrano Valley High School, and a meeting with Sheriff Don Barnes at the Real Time Operation
 Center. She was also pleased to announce that the Character Program won National and International
 recognition and gave a shout out to Pip and Sir Speedy who donate their materials to all 23 schools.
 Lastly, Council Member Kelley stated she attended a recognition luncheon hosted by the American
 Red Cross Orange County Division where the Mission Viejo Marines and Sailors Adoption
 Committee won the Heroes Award for service to the Armed Forces and showed a video highlighting
 their accomplishments. She thanked the committee and residents for their support of the Marines and
 Sailors, and David Engwall form the American Red Cross.

 Council Member Vasquez

 Council Member Vasquez commenced by stating she had a hand in the Election Comments page and
 that a resident actually brought it to her attention, and she passed it along. She also addressed
 comments made pertaining to Judy Bullockus and the inappropriate usage of a certain word. She
 completely understands and appreciates the residents’ reaction; however, stated the Council does not
 have jurisdiction over the matter and suggested maybe reaching out to the Community of Character
 leadership. Council Member Vasquez announced Mission Viejo Pride 2025 will be held on Saturday,
 June 21, at Saddleback College from Noon to 4pm and encouraged all to visit the website https://mv-
 pride.com for more details. She was also pleased to share that the committee has raised over $25,000
 so far this year. She concluded by stating she attended the following events: a tour of the Real Time
 Operations Center in Tustin, Third Grade Environmental Fair, Earth Day/Arbor Day event, and a tour
 of Families Forward Community Market.

City Council Minutes  10  May 13, 2025
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

 Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum commented on the flock cameras and how they are strictly for Law
 Enforcement and crime prevention, working alongside neighboring South County communities to
 create a safer environment. She announced that she too attended the SCAG Conference (Southern
 California Association of Governments), and expressed her gratitude to Long Beach Council Member
 Cindy Allen for reappointed her to the Legislative Executive Committee. This will allow her to
 participate and contribute to providing transportation for the upcoming 2028 Olympics. She thanked
 those who spoke on Love Mission Viejo and all the houses of worship for their involvement. Mayor
 Pro Tem Bucknum attended; Earth Day/Arbor Day event, National Prescription Take Back Day, and
 the Mission Viejo Girls Softball end of season tournament. She reminded everyone of the upcoming
 80’s theme Night Market on Saturday, May 17, the Property Insurance Town Hall meeting on Monday,
 May19, at 5:30pm and Memorial Day Ceremony at Kershaw Gardens on Monday, May 26, at 8am.
 In closing Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum congratulated the Character Committee on their worthy
 recognition.

 Mayor Ruesch

 Mayor Ruesch announced that the website for posting comments on the staggering of districts for
 2026 Election has been developed and will be up in the next day or so. He also had the opportunity to
 present the same presentation he had given to the Chamber of Commerce, to the residents of Sunrise
 Senior Living, and go through the history of the City’s Olympic movement including Council Member
 Goodells legacy. Mayor Ruesch concluded with a thought from Winson Churchill ~ success is not
 final, failure is not fatal, it’s the courage to continue that counts.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:25p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor
Ruesch adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, May 27, 2025, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of May 27, 2025

City Council Minutes  11  May 13, 2025
